### General TotalVI Options

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_batch`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.Obs column name discriminating between your batches.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_size_factor`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Key in adata.obs for size factor information. Instead of using library size as a size factor,
the provided size factor column will be used as offset in the mean of the likelihood.
Assumed to be on linear scale.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_categorical_covariate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys in adata.obs that correspond to categorical data. These covariates can be added in
addition to the batch covariate and are also treated as nuisance factors
(i.e., the model tries to minimize their effects on the latent space).
Thus, these should not be used for biologically-relevant factors that you do _not_ want to correct for.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_continuous_covariate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys in adata.obs that correspond to continuous data. These covariates can be added in
addition to the batch covariate and are also treated as nuisance factors
(i.e., the model tries to minimize their effects on the latent space). Thus, these should not be
used for biologically-relevant factors that you do _not_ want to correct for.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_epochs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of passes through the dataset
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `400`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_query_epochs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of passes through the dataset, when fine-tuning model for query
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `200`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--weight_decay`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Weight decay, when fine-tuning model for query
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--force_retrain`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If true, retrain the model and save it to reference_model_path
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_input`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Boolean .var column to subset data with (e.g. containing highly variable genes). By default, do not subset genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::::

### Clustering options RNA

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_obs_cluster`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Prefix for the .obs keys under which to add the cluster labels. Newly created columns in .obs will
be created from the specified value for '--obs_cluster' suffixed with an underscore and one of the resolutions
resolutions specified in '--leiden_resolution'.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"totalvi_integration_leiden"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_leiden_resolution`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Control the coarseness of the clustering. Higher values lead to more clusters.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/totalvi_scarches_leiden/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/workflows/integration/totalvi_scarches_leiden);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/totalvi_scarches_leiden/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
